title: The Minstrel's Ransom
logline: A holiday concert promoter hires an armed pilot to intercept a beloved acoustic balladeer who is fleeing with the festival deposit to join a rival mining colony.

roles.description: An overextended entertainment factor who mortgaged his family shuttle to organize the solstice concert.
An aging acoustic balladeer whose songs have defined frontier miners for forty years; vain, tired, looking for an honest exit.
A rented heavy patrol craft armed with tractor grapples and EMP disabling arrays.
The casino and entertainment trust controlling tickets and vendor concessions for the holiday.
A competing rim cooperative that offered the minstrel a debt-free retirement villa in exchange for exclusive performances.
The massive transparent pleasure dome on the primary station where thirty thousand miners await the concert.
An unaligned mineral waystation on the system rim where the minstrel's getaway transport is refueling.

public_situation: Thirty thousand ticket-holders gather at {role:solstice_amphitheater}, unaware that {role:celebrated_minstrel} has slipped his mooring and fled.
private_truth: {role:festival_promoter} slipped a lifetime performance indenture into the minstrel's booking contract, forcing the musician to flee for his freedom.

beats.public_change: Stage technicians discover the minstrel's dressing cabin empty while sound checks echo across the cavernous amphitheater.

missions.reason: He needs structural ferrite delivered to shore up temporary speaker gantries while he stalls the angry audience and tracks the singer.
missions.private_fact: He already spent the box office ticket receipts to pay off his personal gambling arrears at the station tables.

beats.public_change: A faint encrypted distress ping broadcasts from the asteroid fringe, revealing the minstrel's ship was intercepted by bounty hunters.

missions.reason: He needs the pilot to scan the fringe asteroid relays and identify which hidden landing bay is harboring the singer's vessel.
missions.private_fact: The singer's acoustic guitar holds the only original copy of the forged booking contract hidden inside its soundboard.

beats.public_change: Privateer skirmishers hired by the syndicate swarm the refuge bay, attempting to breach the singer's docking clamps.

missions.reason: The singer needs the syndicate enforcers driven off and the master electronic contract key recovered from their command gunboat.
missions.private_fact: He composed an entirely new ballad during the chase that mocks the promoter's corrupt booking practices by name.

beats.public_change: {role:promoter_gunboat} enters orbital space above {role:outpost_haven}, charging pulse cannons to disable the singer's engines.

missions.reason: The singer needs the promoter's gunboat broken so his passenger transport can break orbit and reach the rival mining guild safely.
missions.private_fact: The gunboat skipper hails mid-fight offering fifty thousand credits in festival scrip to force the singer back to the amphitheater stage.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot disables the gunboat and secures the singer's flight.
resolutions.summary: {role:celebrated_minstrel} reaches the rival colony safely. {role:festival_promoter} is ruined when the festival crowd riots over the empty stage.

consequences.public_summary: A mercenary broke through syndicate muscle to help a legendary frontier singer escape a predatory festival contract.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot accepts the promoter's payout and forces the singer back to the stage.
resolutions.summary: {role:celebrated_minstrel} performs under armed guard to thunderous applause. {role:festival_promoter} pockets the ticket fortune, and the singer remains bonded for life.

consequences.public_summary: Pilots recount how a hired gun hauled an aging musician back to the stage at gunpoint so the promoters could collect their gate receipts.

resolutions.reached_by: The contract is lost or the pilot abandons the chase.
resolutions.summary: Thirty thousand drunken miners tear down {role:solstice_amphitheater} when midnight passes with no music. Both the singer and promoter flee the sector.

loose_threads.detail: The ticket sales ledger shows eighty percent of advance receipts were diverted to an offshore shell firm forty-eight hours before showtime.
The contract document tucked into the guitar case shows an ink signature applied with an automated plotter machine rather than human hand.
The hull numbering on {role:promoter_gunboat} matches an impounded customs interceptor sold at auction without stripped armaments.

radio_hooks: Solstice concert organizers reassure crowds that sound checks are merely running behind schedule.
Miners pack the amphitheater concourse singing traditional frontier mining laments.
Rival mining outposts broadcast open invitations offering asylum to stranded artists.

voice_direction.festival_promoter: Rapid-fire, oily, and perpetually hysterical. Uses high-energy showmanship to mask intense panic, constantly checking his phone while promising impossible bonuses.
voice_direction.celebrated_minstrel: Deep, weary, and dryly cynical. Speaks with theatrical eloquence when he wants to, but sounds mostly like an exhausted tradesman whose tools have been stolen.
